L'établissement accueille environ 1 340 élèves et compte près de 130 membres du personnel enseignant et administratif. La surface SHON totale est de 14 037 m². Le bâtiment E est de plain-pied (RDC), les bâtiments C et F s'élèvent sur deux niveaux (R+1), tandis que les bâtiments A, B et D atteignent trois niveaux (R+2). title: Ireland – Historical monument or memorial construction work – Monaghan County Council wishes to tender for: Remedial Conservation Works to the Rossmore Memorial Fountain.
description: The project involves remedial conservation works to the Rossmore Memorial Fountain, a protected Victorian Gothic Revival monument (built 1875–76 by Robinson and Son of Belfast) located in The Diamond, Monaghan. The fountain is a significant architectural and historical landmark, originally erected to commemorate Henry Robert Westenra, 4th Baron Rossmore, and funded by public subscription. Project Objectives Stabilise and conserve the monument’s historic masonry and carved stonework, focusing on areas of active deterioration and public safety risks. Preserve original materials and craftsmanship using minimal intervention and reversible, lime-based conservation techniques. Maintain the monument’s role as the architectural centrepiece of Monaghan’s main public square, ensuring public safety and accessibility during works.

title: Disassembly and Relocation of AV-8B Harrier II for the National Museum of the Marine Corps (NMMC)
description: NMMC has a requirement to relocate a McDonnell Douglas AV-8B Harrier II BuNo 165588 from Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Yuma to NMMC. The aircraft is currently being stored on the flight line of MCAS Yuma. It shall be disassembled and loaded at MCAS Yuma and transported to its first destination at MCAS Cherry Point. After the aircraft undergoes restoration at MCAS Cherry Point by Fleet Readiness Center East (FRC), the same aircraft will be loaded at MCAS Cherry Point and delivered to the NMMC Museum Support Facility (MSF) in Dumfries, VA. Please see attached solicitation, technical specifications and PWS for full details. VENDOR QUESTIONS: Questions about this RFQ must be submitted via email to both David Laster and Michael Bogatyr at the following email addresses: michael.bogatyr@usmc.mil; david.laster@usmc.mil. In order to receive a response, the Email Subject Line of the submission must read "M0026426Q0130, Q&A for Harrier Jet Disassembly & Transport". Questions shall be submitted no later than Thursday, August 20th, 2026, at 11:00 AM Eastern Time. No late questions will be accepted. Any resultant responses from Q&A will be posted with the solicitation as an amendment to SAM.gov.

title: Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Expansion
description: he United States Property and Fiscal Office for Pennsylvania intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price purchase order to SUMMIT FIRE & SECURITY LLC for services to expand the Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) and enhance Legacy Bosch Video Management System consisting of analog cameras. Adding additional cameras, upgrading the server, relocating the main server, and replacing all existing analog cameras will be increased to monitor additional designated areas which will increase safety and security of EAATS cadre and students. The period of performance is expected to be six (6) months which includes delivery of materials and equipment, and the installation and integration of all equipment. The reason for this noncompetitive contract action is that SUMMIT FIRE & SECURITY LLC holds the National Guard Bureau (NGB) certifcation required to work on electronic security systems. Electronic Security System contractors doing work for the National Guard are required to have completed the Electronic System Security Course at Camp Robinson, AR. In addition, SUMMIT FIRE & SECURITY LLC has the warranty responsibility on all added systems, maintenance agreement, software licenses, set up and programming responsibility for the existing electronic systems throughout the Pennsylvania National Guard. These services are provided through a contractual agreement between the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's Department of Military and Veteran Affairs and SUMMIT FIRE & SECURITY LLC. This contract action is for services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.106-l(b). This contract action will be awarded following the issuance of written solicitation with an anticipated award date of not later than September 15, 2026.

title: Safe Boat
description: This is for market research purposes ONLY and no award is guaranteed as a result of this sources sought. This is NOT a request for competitive proposals and is published for informational purposes only; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the Government. Moody AFB is looking for vendor capable of providing a 25-Foot commercial-grade rigid-hull, fiberglass-reinforced law enforcement patrol vessel with dual outboard propulsion engines, electronic/navigation system, law enforcement lighting, custom operational accessories and an aluminum trailer. The vessel will be utilized by Port Moody AFB tactical and law enforcement units to conduct waterborne security, patrol, interdiction, and search0and-rescue operations in austere coastal and harbor environments. The following characteristics are as follows Hull Design & Construction: � Must feature an unsinkable hull design utilizing commercial-grade fiberglass construction with high-density foam flotation. � Self-bailing deck cockpit with integrated scuppers. � Minimum cockpit interior freeboard of 28 inches. � Heavy-duty rubrail and heavy-duty rub strakes (angle mount) for structural defense during close-quarters maneuvers and docking. � Stainless steel cutwater guard to protect the keel during shallow or rocky operations. � Length overall (LOA) of approximately 25 feet to balance stability and maneuverability in harbors and coastal zones. Propulsion & Fuel System: � Dual outboard configuration: Dual 225 HP V6 CMS DTS (Digital Throttle & Shift) engines (minimum total 450 HP) to ensure high-speed transit and operational redundancy. � Fuel capacity: Minimum 172-gallon integrated under-deck fuel tank. � Engine guard / crash rail installed around the outboards to prevent damage during tactical boarding or collisions. � Hydraulic tilt steering system with recessed electric trim tabs. Tactical & Mission Equipment: � Heavy-Duty Tow Post: Bow-mounted towing eye and a heavy-duty stern-mounted tow post with storage (must delete standard stern seating to maximize operational deck space). � Weapon Storage: Integrated weapon storage solutions, including a 36-inch aluminum leaning post with built-in secure weapon storage and an associated protective canvas cover. � Scuba Storage: Custom-mounted scuba cylinder rack capable of securing a minimum of four (4) SCUBA bottles, plus integrated rod holders at the helm seat and stern deck. Navigation & Communications Electronics: � Primary Display: Minimum 16" Simrad NSO EVO3S (or functional equivalent) multi-function electronics and navigation display package. � Radar: Simrad Dome HALO24 (or functional equivalent) high-definition marine radar system mounted to the hardtop. � Sonar: 1kW thru-hull transducer for precision depth and sub-surface imaging. � VHF Radio: Marine VHF radio system (Simrad RS40 or functional equivalent) with external antenna. � Thermal Night Vision: Pan-Tilt-Zoom thermal night vision camera system (M332-30HZ or functional equivalent) integrated with the primary display (hardtop-mounted). Law Enforcement & Tactical Lighting: � Emergency Lighting: Whelen (or functional equivalent) law enforcement emergency marine lighting package (Cenator 36" hardtop-mounted lightbar) featuring high-intensity LED lights, siren, and speaker system. Configured with RED/Amber tactical lighting. � Searchlight: Hardtop-mounted ACR remote-controlled spotlight (minimum 200,000 candlepower) operated from the console helm. � Tactical Underwater Lights: Minimum of three (3) blue LED high-intensity underwater transom lights for low-visibility operations and tactical diving support. Consoles, Shelter & Comfort: � Center console configuration with protective hardtop frame, electronic box (E-box), and integrated windshield wiper. � Leaning post with flip-up bolster and backrest for the helm operator. � Full weather wing curtains (attaching to the hardtop) to protect operators from inclement weather. � Bow area seat cushions with forward console base and backrest for transport and rescue personnel. � Reversible helm seat with raw water plumbing (fill and drain capability). Required Accessories & Covers The vessel package must include the following custom-fit protective canvas covers and operational support gear to maintain readiness: � One (1) 36" Leaning Post / Weapon Storage canvas cover (Black). � One (1) Console protective cover (Black). � One (1) Leaning Post cover (Black). � One (1) integrated battery charging system with a heavy-duty battery package (minimum three (3) GR31 AGM marine-grade batteries) and two (2) fire extinguishers. � One (1) complete anchor package (marine-grade anchor, chain, and line rated for vessel size). Trailer Requirements � Type: Heavy-duty, dual-axle aluminum boat trailer (specifically designed to fit a 25-foot rigid commercial hull). � Brakes & Lights: Integrated marine-grade braking system and waterproof LED road lighting. � Capacity: Sized appropriately to support the dry weight of the vessel, dual engines, fuel load, and mission equipment. Warranty and Delivery � Hull Warranty: Minimum ten (10) year limited commercial hull warranty. � Engine Warranty: Manufacturer standard commercial warranty for dual outboards. � Manuals: Complete set of digital operator, parts, engine, and electronics maintenance manuals. � Delivery: Inland freight and handling included to the designated Port Moody AFB drop-off point. All questions or comments related to this Sources Sought shall be directed to the Contract Specialist, SSgt Kevin Goris at kevin.goris@us.af.mil.

title: Hungarian Payroll and Social Security Tax Administration Services
description: PR16205463 - Hungarian Payroll and Social Security Tax Administration Services The U.S. Embassy in Budapest, Hungary requires comprehensive personal income tax, social security, and pension contribution calculation, deduction, reporting, and advisory services for its locally employed Hungarian staff, in full compliance with Hungarian Tax Legislation, the National Tax and Customs Administration of Hungary, and Hungarian Social Security regulations. The Contractor shall mainly provide payroll administration and tax compliance services for Hungarian employees on a bi-weekly payroll schedule (26 periods per year). The contract period is planned for 1 calendar year, from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2027, with 3 consecutive optional years exercisable at the sole discretion of the U.S. Government. Examples of the services the provider will be expected to deliver: Payroll processing and calculations (wage calculations, bi-weekly payroll and tax calculations utilizing automated software, e.g., NEXON or equivalent, etc.) Social security and health insurance administration (assessing eligibility, calculating health insurance and social security allowances, maintaining statutory records, etc.) Employee master data management (onboarding, offboarding, tax declarations, operational calendars, etc.) Regulatory reporting and statutory filings (communication with NAV and Social Security authorities, submitting mandatory filings and forms, preparing statistics and documents, etc.) Audit assistance, revisions, employee briefings and trainings, etc. All firms that respond to this solicitation must be technically qualified and financially responsible to perform such services. At a minimum, each offeror must meet the following requirements to submit a proposal: Have an established business with a permanent address and telephone listing in Hungary Be able to understand written and spoken English Have the necessary personnel, equipment, and financial resources available to perform the work, including trained and qualified payroll technicians Have all licenses and permits required by local, Hungarian law Have liability insurance Contractual Framework The contracting party shall be the U.S. Embassy in Hungary, a diplomatic mission of the United States of America, and not a Hungarian commercial entity. Contracts awarded by the Embassy are governed by applicable U.S. federal acquisition laws and regulations, including the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Department of State Acquisition Regulation (DOSAR), as well as applicable international agreements, including the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations. The Embassy will issue its own U.S. Government Purchase Order as the contractual instrument. The Embassy will not execute or accept a contractor's standard Hungarian contract, terms and conditions, or other contractual form in lieu of the U.S. Government Purchase Order.

title: S2 Cognition
description: Title: S2 Cognition Description: The 5th Special Forces Group (Airborne) at Fort Campbell, KY, requires a one-year license agreement for a comprehensive Cognitive Performance Assessment System. This system is essential for evaluating and enhancing the cognitive abilities of Special Forces operators, which are critical for mission success in high-stress, dynamic environments. The required solution includes the provision of a scientifically validated cognitive testing platform, all necessary hardware, software licenses, and related support services. The primary objective is to measure and analyze the cognitive processes that underlie rapid, split-second decision-making. Questions are due August 31, 2026 1400 CST. Responses are due September 07, 2026 1000 CST. Key Requirements: Cognitive Assessment: The system must be a computer-based testing platform capable of measuring cognitive performance with millisecond precision. It must assess at least thirteen specific cognitive domains, including but not limited to perception speed, search efficiency, decision complexity, and impulse control. Hardware and Software: The contractor shall provide all necessary equipment, including testing consoles, monitors, and peripherals, along with the required software licenses, maintenance, and updates. Data and Analysis: The solution must include secure database storage for all assessment results and provide consultation services for score interpretation relative to Special Operations roles. Validation: The testing protocols and equipment must be scientifically based, using statistically validated methods, and demonstrate test-retest reliability. This is a brand-name requirement for the "S2 Cognition" system. Offerors must propose the specified brand-name product to be considered technically acceptable. Quotes for alternate or "equal" products will not be accepted. For a complete list of requirements and salient characteristics, please refer to the attached solicitation documents.

title: Ireland – Health services – NTPF Establishment of a Framework of Private Healthcare Providers for the Provision of Additional Healthcare Capacity
description: The National Treatment Purchase Fund (the “NTPF”) hereby invites suitably qualified and experienced Healthcare Providers to submit tenders for the establishment of a Multiparty Framework of Private Healthcare Providers for the Provision of Additional Inpatient and Outpatient services (the “Framework”). This procurement is being conducted under the Light Touch Regime applicable to social and other specific services pursuant to the European Union (Award of Public Authority Contracts) Regulations 2016 (S.I. No. 284/2016), as amended, and the relevant provisions of Directive 2014/24/EU. The procurement is being conducted using the Open Procedure and is subject to the applicable requirements and principles of equal treatment, non-discrimination, transparency, proportionality and competition. The NTPF may specify service volumes and implementation arrangements through Call-Off Contracts awarded in accordance with the Framework Agreement and the procurement documents. The NTPF wishes to appoint Healthcare Provider(s) for each of the Lots indicated below. Tenderers will be invited to submit for one, some or all six Lots. • Lot 1: Adult Day Case Procedures • Lot 2: Adult Inpatient Procedures • Lot 3: Adult Outpatient Services including minor OP Procedures • Lot 4: Paediatric Day Case Procedures • Lot 5: Paediatric Inpatient Procedures • Lot 6: Paediatric Outpatient Services including minor OP Procedures The NTPF intends to appoint more than one Healthcare Provider for each of the Lots. The NTPF intends to operate this Framework across the Lots and certain minimum mandatory suitability requirements will be specified at the mini-competition stage and not the Framework invitation stage. Note: Healthcare Providers are requested to only submit a tender if they are confident that they have the requisite capacity, suitably qualified staff, experience and expertise within their organisation to deliver on the service as outlined in the tender documentation commencing as soon as practicable after award of contract. All submissions will be reviewed for compliance with the specifications as outlined in this document. Framework: This procurement is being conducted under the Open Procedure pursuant to the applicable public procurement regulations. Tenderers will be assessed against the Mandatory Framework Admission Requirements and Minimum Mandatory Suitability Requirements set out in the procurement documentation. All tenderers that meet these requirements and submit compliant tenders will be admitted to the framework agreement. Tenderers that do not meet the stated requirements or whose tenders are otherwise deemed non-compliant will not be admitted to the framework. There shall be no limit on the number of economic operators admitted to the Framework. Following establishment of the framework, as and when requirements for the Services arise, it is anticipated that the NTPF will award Call-Off Contracts by way of a Mini-Competition. Contract Duration: 24 Months with 2 x 12-month extension periods.

title: Ireland – Construction work – RFT 02/26/GM - Works Contractor and PSCS for ATU Dublin Road EEDPP2 Energy Retrofit at Atlantic Technological University at the Galway City Campus
description: Atlantic Technological University (ATU) is seeking suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake an energy retrofit project at its Galway City Dublin Road Campus. The project comprises the retrofit of approximately 4,425m² of the original 1972 building and forms part of the Higher Education Authority (HEA) and Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) funded Energy Efficiency and Decarbonisation Pathfinder Project (EEDPP2). The works include building fabric upgrades, roof and window replacement, ventilation improvements, lighting and controls upgrades, and the installation of a medium-temperature air-source heat pump, with existing gas boilers retained for peak demand and backup. The project aims to improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, extend the building's operational life, enhance occupant comfort, increase the use of renewable technologies, and achieve a minimum B1 BER rating. The existing building is a reinforced concrete framed structure currently served by the campus central heating system and a combination of natural and mechanical ventilation systems.

title: Data Transmission Network (DTN) HS2
description: The HS2 Data Transmission Network (DTN) will provide network transport services and specific central service functions necessary for the reliable operation of trains on HS2. The DTN shall fulfil the following high-level requirements: • Provision of a Critical network for safety-related connected sub-systems: DTN-Critical • Provision of a Protected network (DTN-P), distinct from the critical DTN network, connecting non-safety-related subsystems. • Provision of a secure, geo-redundant external interface via a De-Militarized Zone (DMZ). DTN acts as the aggregator for internet and cloud connectivity from its DMZ. The DTN DMZ also acts as the interface to Network Rail to connect HS2 rail systems to Conventional Rail services hosted in Network Rail's telecoms network. • Provision of the DMZ, including central compute and servers, protected by internal and external security perimeters. • Provision of a Master Clock System, providing accurate clocking internally and to connected subsystems with Precision Time Protocol (PTP) with boundary clock functionality, Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE), and Network Time Protocol (NTP). • Provision of other services include: DHCP, DNS, AAA authentication, Network Management System (NMS) for supplied operational systems. • Provision of optical and electrical SFP (where required) to facilitate the above inter-connectivity.

title: Sole Source Chapter PomePlex-26 NGS Assay (96 tests)
description: Sole Source Notification Acquisition of 10 kits of the ChapterDx PomePlex 26 The Plant Germplasm Quarantine Program routinely screens for a battery of 26 viruses and viroids through individual PCR diagnostics for each of the 26 targets, which is very laborious and time consuming. The ChapterDx PomePlex 26 allows testing all 26 viruses and viroids all at once in a single tube reaction. This technology will be used as part of the work plan approved for a project awarded by the Plant Protection Act PPA7721 Spending plan FY26 titled �Implementing a largescale assay for simultaneous diagnostic of all pome tree viruses/viroids in certification programs�. The list of awarded projects can be found at Plant Protection Act Section 7721 Fiscal Year 2026 Spending Plan. Each of the 10 kits requested for purchasing provides enough reagents to conduct diagnostics on 96 individual samples across the 26 targeted plant pathogens. ChapterDx is the only company that sells a 26 NGS assay ready for sequencing in a 96 sample format with as little as 2ul of samples when followed NGS-based techniques. Our laboratory conducts plant pathogen diagnostics of imported germplasm that are compatible with all our established workflows for accurate diagnostics of plant pathogens using the ChapterDx Pome Plex 26 NGS assay. This notice closes September 07, 2026 12:00 PM CST Todd K. title: Sources Sought - Fluorescence Microscope
description: Sources Sought #1172160-SS This is a Sources Sought notice Only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only as part of USDA ARS market research and does not itself constitute an RFQ. General Information The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service, Houma, LA has a need for a Compound Microscope (Olympus BX53) with Phase Contrast and Fluorescent Capabilities. This instrumentation is vital for investigating infection mechanisms through the use of fluorescent protein-tagged fungal and bacterial pathogens in sugarcane, as well as for routine disease diagnosis and pathogen morphology study. Timely identification and study of pathogen introduction are critical to preventing disease establishment and developing management strategies that support farmers, stakeholders, and the overall sugarcane industry. Thus, this instrument is vital in day-to-day laboratory activities. The requested Olympus BX53 from Evident/Olympus is the only known configuration that meets these specific technical requirements. Detailed product specifications and requirements are attached. This Sources Sought is only for the purpose of identifying potential sources as part of USDA ARS market research. The Government does not intend to make an award based on responses to this inquiry. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources including any Small Businesses; HUBZone small business; service-disabled, veteran-owned small business; 8(a) small business; veteran-owned small business; woman-owned small business; and small disadvantaged businesses. This is also to obtain information on the availability of domestically available end-products. Please state if you are a large business or a small business according to the NAICS code listed in this Sources Sought. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response defines how it can specifically meet the specifications for the items requested. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After reviewing the responses received, a Combined Synopsis Solicitation notice may be published on Sam.gov. Submit ALL the Following in order to be a valid response to this Sources Sought Notice: 1. Capability Statement that demonstrates your ability to meet all of the specific requirements of Statement of Work and must include Company Contact Info. 2. SAM.gov UEI Number. 3. Country of origin for the product Original Point of Contact: All responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be received by September 7, 2026 by 12:00 PM ET, the specified due date and time to be considered and must include all items requested above. title: B--Notice of Intent
description: The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) intends to award a sole source contract s stable isotope ratio analysis of carbon, oxygen, and nitrogen from powdered calcium carbonate samples to Iowa State University. description: THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR EITHER A QUOTE OR PROPOSAL, OR AN INVITATION FOR BID.THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL CRANE PARTS AND COMPONENTS CAPABLE OF MEETING THE AGENCY�S REQUIREMENTS. The purpose of this notice is to determine if there are commercially available crane parts and components that demonstrate the ability to meet the Agency�s requirements. The crane part and component would potentially be specified (as brand name) within the Base Operating Support Contract (BOSC) issued for services to repair Capstan located at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay within the NAVFAC Southeast Area of Responsibility. Looking for parts which have capability with Capstan 87-00034. These parts must comply with the requirements of the NAVFAC P-307 Weight Handling Program Management for compatible maintenance and replacement parts for this type of Capstan. The Agency�s requirement for the part and component includes a Stearns Brake Model 82,000 Series 330 ft-lbs brake P/N 1-082-042-02-261. Interested and responsible parties are to respond to this to this inquiry by 7 September 2026. If you have, please describe the brand/type and any obstacles/successes. title: Bottle Field Assessment
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a commercial service prepared in accordance with the format in the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) subpart 12.202, as supplemented with additional information. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all offers received in response to this solicitation. Furthermore, the Government maintains the right to not make an award under this solicitation, and reserves the unilateral right to cancel this solicitation, in whole or in part, at any point prior to award if it is determined to be in the Government's best interest. All solicitation provisions and contract clauses applicable to this procurement are incorporated and set forth in Attachment 2 � SF 1449. Submission of a quote constitutes acknowledgement and acceptance of all terms contained within this attachment. The Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC) Hypervelocity Wind Tunnel 9 in White Oak, Maryland, requires a comprehensive Engineering Assessment of nineteen (19) high-pressure gaseous nitrogen (GN2) storage vessels, collectively known as the "Bottle Field." The objective is to determine the optimal and continued safe operating condition of the facility. The contractor shall perform a multi-phased assessment (Parts I through V) encompassing data collection, Non-Destructive Examination (NDE) plan development and on-site execution, Finite Element Analysis (FEA), and a Minimum Design Metal Temperature (MDMT) evaluation. All engineering analysis must be conducted in strict accordance with API 579 / ASME FFS-1 standards for pressure vessels operating at or above 10,000 psig. See Attachment 1 - Statement of Work (SOW) for full details.

title: Principal Multi-Domain Command & Control (MDC2) Subject Matter Expert
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Command, Control, Communications, and Battle Management (PAE C3BM), Operational Response Team (ORT) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis to conduct market research and identify potential sources capable of providing highly specialized Principal Multi-Domain Command & Control (MDC2) Subject Matter Expertise (SME) support. 2.0 REQUIREMENT OVERVIEW The primary objective of this effort is to facilitate the seamless tactical integration of Common Operating Picture and Common Tactical Picture (COP/CTP) architectures into the tactical edge of the Department of the Air Force Battle Network (DAFBN) and Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS). The Government is seeking industry capabilities regarding Principal MDC2 SMEs with a minimum of 10 years of extensive background in: Space superiority C2 systems (e.g., Kronos) and integrated space coordination (DARPA ABII). Priority kill-chain constructs across rapid acquisition (Space RCO), missile defense, and national intelligence. Development of GEO Rendezvous and Proximity Operations (RPO) planning tools. Multi-source sensemaking, automated Course of Action (CoA) generation, and on-orbit edge processing (Nebula/Space Cloud). Security Requirement: This effort requires personnel to possess active Top Secret (TS) clearances with Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) eligibility, the ability to be read into Special Access Programs (SAPs), and access to an ICD 705 accredited facility. 3.0 IMPORTANT NOTE TO INDUSTRY (CROSS-REFERENCE) The Government is concurrently releasing a separate RFI for Tactical Aviation SME Support. This specific notice is strictly for the Principal MDC2 SME (Space/Orbital C2) requirement. Please ensure you are reviewing the correct PWS and responding to the correct notice. 4.0 ATTACHMENTS Interested vendors must review the attached documents for full requirement details and submission instructions: Attachment 1: Request for Information (RFI) Attachment 2: Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) 5.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS This is an RFI only. This does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an indication that the Government will contract for the services discussed. All information submitted is strictly voluntary. Responses shall follow the formatting, page limits, and instruction guidelines detailed in Attachment 1 (RFI). title: MARKET SURVEY/ SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR Horlick Dam Removal and Root River Restoration
description: General. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT and is for informational/market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTATION OR BID, NOR A SYNOPSIS OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION UNDER FAR SUBPART 5.2 By way of this Market Survey/Sources Sought Notice, the USACE-Chicago District intends to determine the extent of firms that are engaged in providing the services described hereunder for the Horlick Dam Removal on the Root River at River Mile 5.3 in Racine, Wisconsin. The responses to this Notice will be used for planning purposes for an upcoming procurement. Therefore, this Notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP); it does not guarantee the future issue of an RFP; nor does it commit the government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, this Agency will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that this Agency will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice; all costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the responding party expense. At this time, proprietary information is not being requested, and respondents shall refrain from providing proprietary information in response to this Notice. Responses to this Notice will not be returned. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Notice does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. In accordance with RFO FAR 15.101(c), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this Notice. GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENTS: Under the proposed Contract, the contractor will be required to provide the following construction services: The project consists of the controlled removal of Horlick Dam on the Root River at River Mile 5.3 in Racine, Wisconsin. The work includes the gradual drawdown of the impoundment through the staged removal of the existing stop logs, demolition and removal of the dam structure, and stabilization of the downstream retaining wall using riprap. The objective of the project is to safely remove the existing hydraulic structure, restore natural river flow through the project area, and provide a stable downstream channel following dam removal. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidentals necessary to complete the work in accordance with the contract drawings, specifications, and applicable permits. The Contractor shall develop and implement a controlled reservoir drawdown plan, monitor site conditions throughout the drawdown period, demolish and remove the existing dam structure, transport and dispose of demolition materials, and install riprap stabilization along the downstream retaining wall as specified. Temporary flow management, erosion and sediment control, and protection of adjacent infrastructure shall be provided for the duration of construction. The Contractor shall demonstrate experience performing hydraulic structure demolition, controlled reservoir drawdowns, in-water construction, and heavy civil construction activities. The Contractor shall also demonstrate the capability to safely execute the work while complying with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permit requirements. Estimated Performance Period: 365 calendar days Estimated Cost: Between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00 Estimated Solicitation: February 2027 Estimated Award: April 2027. The VA Medical Center, Manchester, NH (VAMCMNH) requires new standardized interior wayfinding signage to improve the ease with which Veterans and visitors navigate the campus. The intent is to update all directional signs to a uniform standard that improves visibility and clarity, and that coordinates with newly installed exterior signage. 3.1 Objectives VAMCMNH requires a turnkey wayfinding signage project. The Contractor shall design an overall wayfinding system, including departmental identification, directional, and ADA-compliant signage; fabricate; remove existing signage; and install new interior signage throughout the main building (approximately 290,000 SF, 7 stories, 3 major public entrances). The design shall standardize and unify signage using colors, symbols (Eagle, Mountain, and Seacoast motifs), cardinal points, and text, with field-replaceable inserts capable of in-house reprinting. The Contractor shall propose how the Medical Center's existing electronic directories at the three main entrances can be integrated into the overall wayfinding design. Signage shall leverage the facility's spatial organization and architectural features (destination zones, landmarks, shape, color). Signage shall be easy to recognize, consistent, clear, distinctive, and legible. Signage shall comply with current ADA/ABA Accessible Design Standards where required. The Contractor's signage shall be unified with existing exterior and retained interior signage. Finalize all sign system design elements, fabrication specifications, graphics, and installation details. Prepare sign layouts based on final message schedules to determine sign/letter sizing. Provide final fabrication submittals based on approved design. Remove existing signage requiring removal; perform wall prep and repair (VA will supply paint). All shop drawings and material samples shall be submitted to the COR for approval before fabrication. title: Attending Veterinarian (AV) Services for the Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) Environmental Laboratory (EL) Animal Care and Use Program
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), Environmental Laboratory (EL) in Vicksburg, MS, is issuing this Presolicitation / Sources Sought Notice to identify qualified and interested sources capable of providing non-personal Attending Veterinarian (AV) services. This notice is part of market research to determine the availability of qualified small and large business contractors, as well as to seek industry feedback on the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). GENERAL INFORMATION & INSTRUCTIONS 1. Purpose of this Notice The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), Environmental Laboratory (EL) in Vicksburg, MS, is issuing this Presolicitation / Sources Sought Notice to identify qualified and interested sources capable of providing non-personal Attending Veterinarian (AV) services. This notice is part of market research to determine the availability of qualified small and large business contractors, as well as to seek industry feedback on the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). 2. Acquisition Strategy The Government intends to issue a competitive solicitation for these services. This notice requests the submission of capability statements from interested parties to verify the pool of qualified contractors and to assist in finalized acquisition planning. 3. Submission Requirements for Capability Statements Interested firms must submit a Capability Statement (not to exceed 5 pages, excluding resume/license attachments) demonstrating their ability to perform the services outlined in the draft PWS. Submissions must include the following information: A. Company Profile Company Name, Address, and Website. Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE Code. Business Size and Type under NAICS 541940 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HubZone, Large Business). Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone Number, and Email). B. Technical Capability & Qualification Criteria Vendors must explicitly address and provide proof of the following mandatory qualifications: Professional Degree: Provide proof of a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM or VMD) degree from an AVMA-accredited institution. Professional Licensure: Provide proof of active, unrestricted licensure to practice veterinary medicine in the State of Mississippi. Core Experience: Provide a detailed narrative or resume demonstrating a minimum of five (5) years of experience serving as an Attending Veterinarian (AV) within an AAALAC-accredited laboratory animal care and use program. Species Expertise: Detail specific scientific experience in laboratory animal science/medicine and the care of specific species maintained by ERDC-EL (including aquatic, amphibian, reptilian, and avian species, as well as mammalian wildlife species as applicable to environmental research). Geographic Proximity: Confirm that the primary base of operations is located within 200 miles one way of the ERDC-EL facilities in Vicksburg, MS, to meet the mandatory 4-hour emergency on-site response window. C. Past Performance Provide up to three (3) references for similar services performed within the past five (5) years. Include the contract number, client organization, a brief description of the scope, and a reference contact (name, phone, and email). 4. How to Submit Please submit your capability statements electronically via email to the Contract Specialist at Derek Howard at Derek.A.Howard@usace.army.mil CHL-CT-QUOTES@usace.army.mil no later than the response deadline indicated above. The email subject line must read: "Response to Presolicitation Notice W912HZ24R3737 � ERDC-EL AV Services"

title: C1DA--A/E Services Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT Project Number: 662-25-105
description: This is a Call for SF 330s. Please read the entire document. The Department of Veterans Affairs VA San Francisco Healthcare System, CA is seeking Architectural/Engineering Firms to submit Standard Form (SF) 330 for Project 662-25-105, Design Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT. The project will be located at the San Francisco VA Campus, 4150 Clement St, San Francisco, California 94121. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The requirement is for Project 662-25-105 Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT at the San Francisco VA Medical Center, Building 203 Ground Floor A-Wing, to provide A/E design services to renovate 13,750 SF of existing Outpatient Mental Health, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and VA Police Service space into a modern Hemodialysis Clinic and Women's Clinic plus renovated police and specialty care areas, supporting the long-term plan to consolidate inpatient care to the 2nd and 3rd floors, with an estimated construction cost of $15.7M, requiring a 2-day on-site design charrette, site investigations, block diagrams, and full design deliverables at 35%, 65%, 95%, 100% and final production per VA Master Specs and all applicable codes, including cost estimates, phased construction documents, and 5-year construction period services including RFI responses, submittal reviews, weekly meetings, site inspections, and as-builts, all to be completed within a 400-day design period. The design shall also substantially meet the VA design criteria as listed in VA design guides and manuals which can be found on the web at the VA Office of Facilities Management technical information library site address; http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL The design effort shall also include review of and assurance of compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act, including development and submission of all documents, reports, and activities necessary to obtain the required compliance. The contract work requires multiple disciplines. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm, and the lead designer in each discipline must be registered but neither need to be registered in California. The disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Interior Design, Structural, HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, Fire Protection, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Wayfinding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Include any additional disciplines that may be necessary on the SF 330. SF 330 Part 1F Example Projects; present all relevant VA projects first. Include in block 21 the contract number for all federal projects. Do not include the CPARS reports for federal projects. SELECTION CRITERIA Selection of firms for interviews and negotiations shall be based on an evaluation of the submitted SF 330s on the basis of the selection criteria listed below in a descending order of precedence. SF-330 s, Part I may be accompanied by any other evidence of experience and capabilities the applicant considers relevant. Part II shall be submitted for each proposed consultant s office involved. Selection Criteria descriptions are provided below. Past Experience of the prime firm, consultant firms and proposed designers. Prime firms must have proven experience in health care design through construction administration. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence in hospital design with the ability to design and administer projects within a complex, active healthcare environment with stringent seismic requirements in the State of California. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time and the ability to adhere to schedules. Provide current workload capability of the prime firm, proposed consultants and designers. Literature should be included to demonstrate the prime firm s ability to meet scheduled deadlines. This will allow the Government to determine the availability of experienced personnel during the performance period of the contract as well as the capacity to complete the work required. Past Performance on contracts with respect to cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules during design and construction phases (prime firm). Geographical location and knowledge of the locality of the project. This requirement considers the prime firm s familiarity with the applicable geographic area s architectural standards and codes, building codes, environmental regulations, soil conditions, and seismic requirements within the San Francisco area. The prime firm must be able to respond to and be on-site within a twenty-four-hour window. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: No more than eighty (80) pages Font size no smaller than 10 Size of emails not to exceed 10 MB. If more than one email is sent, number emails in subject line as 1 of 2, 2 of 2. Completed and return VAAR 852.219-77 VA Notice of limitation on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (attached) Subject line of the email shall state Company Name | Response to 36C26126R0065 | email 1 of 2 (if necessary) In the body of the email include Prime Company Name; UEI Number, email address and phone number of primary point of contact DUE DATE FOR SF 330 Firms that meet the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit required SF 330 s by 12:00 P.M. Pacific Standard Time (PST) Monday, September 7, 2026, to Alex Arter at alex.arter@va.gov. It is the intent of the Contracting Officer to make a single firm-fixed price contract award under this solicitation.

title: Injectable Influenza Vaccine
description: The Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support is soliciting for the supply of Injectable Influenza Vaccine for the 2027-2028 flu season. Approximately 1.5 million doses are included in this requirement. (Quantities may increase or decrease pending receipt of final Service requirements.) The vaccines shall be in prefilled syringes presentation. The vaccine shall be FDA-approved for the following age categories: for immunizing individuals 65 years and older, for immunizing individuals 18 years and older, for immunizing individuals 3 years and older, and for immunizing 6 months to 35 months (pediatric group). The formula for the 2027-2028 season shall be determined by the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee. Other specification data is included in the solicitation. Successful contractor must have FDA Approval, and the vaccine must be U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended. National Stock Numbers shall be established at the time of award. An indefinite quantity contract is proposed. The quantity indicated is an annual estimate only. The guaranteed minimum will be 75% of the annual estimate, and a contract maximum will be established at 150% of the annual estimate. All quantities shall be delivered to the Defense Depot New Cumberland, PA. The contractor shall be capable of delivering 40% of the requirement by August 12, 2027, 25% by August 26, 2027, 25% by September 9, 2027, and the residual 10% by September 23, 2027. This delivery schedule is the preferred delivery schedule. Other delivery schedules may be considered. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and SAM.gov at https://www.sam.gov. Interested parties should contact Rosbert Jones (445-737-1254) (Rosbert.Jones@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of presolicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current projected solicitation date is October of 2026. DLA reserves the right to issue the solicitation before or after the projected solicitation date.

title: NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant
description: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Upper Colorado Basin (UCB) Region, Four Corners Construction Office (FCCO), is issuing this Sources Sought notice to determine the availability and capability of small business sources for a contemplated construction project titled: Navajo-Gallup Water Supply Project (NGWSP) Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant. The NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant is located approximately 26-miles South of Bloomfield, New Mexico in San Juan County. This notice is a tool to identify small businesses that have both the technical expertise and bonding capability to accomplish the work required for NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant as the prime contractor and is for informational purposes only. Information obtained through this notice may be used to determine the potential for issuing a future solicitation for this project as a total small business set-aside, and to provide input for the Governments overall acquisition strategy. The NGWSP is a major infrastructure project that once constructed, will convey a reliable municipal and industrial water supply from the San Juan River to the eastern section of the Navajo Nation, southwestern portion of the Jicarilla Apache Nation, and the city of Gallup, New Mexico via about 300 miles of pipeline, 19 pumping plants, and two water treatment plants. This is NOT a Request for Proposals or an Invitation for Bids and does not constitute any commitment by the Government. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this notice. All interested sources must respond to future solicitation announcements separately from responses to the sources sought notice. The NAICS code for this project is 237110 Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction, with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: Draft (90%) Specifications & Drawings have been attached to this Sources Sought notice. The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Upper Colorado Region, Four Corners Construction Office, has a requirement for construction of the Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant of the NGWSP. The principal components of work include the following items: 1. Pre-engineered concrete booster pump station, concrete foundation pad, pipe encasement, yard pipe, fencing, electrical equipment, gravel surfacing, and pipe connections. 2. Installation of secondary regulation tank at Regulation Tank No. 3 site, foundation, electrical equipment, yard pipe, and pipe connections. 3. Erosion and scour restoration/prevention: a. Includes a retaining wall, swale, runoff channel, and site regrading. 4. Reinstallation of gravel surfacing at Regulation Tank No. 3 site. 5. Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) equipment and radio communications system. The estimated magnitude of this project is between $10,000,000 and $25,000.000. LOCATION OF THE WORK: The NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant is located approximately 26-miles South of Bloomfield, off County Road 7575 near U.S. Highway 550, at the base of Huerfano Mesa in San Juan County, New Mexico. INFORMATION REQUESTED: When responding to this notice, respondents are asked to provide the following information: 1. Firms name, address, point of contact, phone number, email address, Cage Code, UEI number. 2. Business classification, to include size and any additional socioeconomic classification(s) (example: SDVOSB, ISBEE, WOSB, etc.). 3. Bonding capability, including current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. Include a letter from your surety to show bonding capability. 4. Brief capabilities statement that addresses experience performing similar projects as a prime contractor. 5. Listing of at least three to a maximum of five previous and/or current projects where the firm has successfully performed similar work. Describe the size and scope of the project(s), and dollar value of the contract. Identify percentage of work on the project(s) that was self-performed. Short responses are appreciated, no need to provide verbose past performance information. SUBMIT TO: Responses to this Sources Sought notice should be received no later than 1 pm Mountain Time on September 7,2026. Submit responses by email to the attention of Philoma Singer, Contract Specialist, Email: philoma_singer@ios.doi.gov and Tyler Spencer, Contracting Officer, Email: tyler_spencer@ios.doi.gov.

title: C1DA--A/E Services Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT Project Number: 662-25-105
description: This is a Call for SF 330s. Please read the entire document. The Department of Veterans Affairs VA San Francisco Healthcare System, CA is seeking Architectural/Engineering Firms to submit Standard Form (SF) 330 for Project 662-25-105, Design Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT. The project will be located at the San Francisco VA Campus, 4150 Clement St, San Francisco, California 94121. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The requirement is for Project 662-25-105 Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT at the San Francisco VA Medical Center, Building 203 Ground Floor A-Wing, to provide A/E design services to renovate 13,750 SF of existing Outpatient Mental Health, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and VA Police Service space into a modern Hemodialysis Clinic and Women's Clinic plus renovated police and specialty care areas, supporting the long-term plan to consolidate inpatient care to the 2nd and 3rd floors, with an estimated construction cost of $15.7M, requiring a 2-day on-site design charrette, site investigations, block diagrams, and full design deliverables at 35%, 65%, 95%, 100% and final production per VA Master Specs and all applicable codes, including cost estimates, phased construction documents, and 5-year construction period services including RFI responses, submittal reviews, weekly meetings, site inspections, and as-builts, all to be completed within a 400-day design period. The design shall also substantially meet the VA design criteria as listed in VA design guides and manuals which can be found on the web at the VA Office of Facilities Management technical information library site address; http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL The design effort shall also include review of and assurance of compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act, including development and submission of all documents, reports, and activities necessary to obtain the required compliance. The contract work requires multiple disciplines. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm, and the lead designer in each discipline must be registered but neither need to be registered in California. The disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Interior Design, Structural, HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, Fire Protection, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Wayfinding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Include any additional disciplines that may be necessary on the SF 330. SF 330 Part 1F Example Projects; present all relevant VA projects first. Include in block 21 the contract number for all federal projects. Do not include the CPARS reports for federal projects. SELECTION CRITERIA Selection of firms for interviews and negotiations shall be based on an evaluation of the submitted SF 330s on the basis of the selection criteria listed below in a descending order of precedence. SF-330 s, Part I may be accompanied by any other evidence of experience and capabilities the applicant considers relevant. Part II shall be submitted for each proposed consultant s office involved. Selection Criteria descriptions are provided below. Past Experience of the prime firm, consultant firms and proposed designers. Prime firms must have proven experience in health care design through construction administration. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence in hospital design with the ability to design and administer projects within a complex, active healthcare environment with stringent seismic requirements in the State of California. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time and the ability to adhere to schedules. Provide current workload capability of the prime firm, proposed consultants and designers. Literature should be included to demonstrate the prime firm s ability to meet scheduled deadlines. This will allow the Government to determine the availability of experienced personnel during the performance period of the contract as well as the capacity to complete the work required. Past Performance on contracts with respect to cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules during design and construction phases (prime firm). Geographical location and knowledge of the locality of the project. This requirement considers the prime firm s familiarity with the applicable geographic area s architectural standards and codes, building codes, environmental regulations, soil conditions, and seismic requirements within the San Francisco area. The prime firm must be able to respond to and be on-site within a four-hour window. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: No more than forty (80) pages Font size no smaller than 10 Size of emails not to exceed 10 MB. If more than one email is sent, number emails in subject line as 1 of 2, 2 of 2. Completed and return VAAR 852.219-77 VA Notice of limitation on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (attached) Subject line of the email shall state Company Name | Response to 36C26122R0061 | email 1 of 2 (if necessary) In the body of the email include Prime Company Name; UEI Number, email address and phone number of primary point of contact DUE DATE FOR SF 330 Firms that meet the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit required SF 330 s by 3:00 P.M. Pacific Standard Time (PST) Monday, September 7, 2026, to Alex Arter at alex.arter@va.gov. It is the intent of the Contracting Officer to make a single firm-fixed price contract award under this solicitation.

title: C1DA--A/E Services Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT Project Number: 662-25-105
description: This is a Call for SF 330s. Please read the entire document. The Department of Veterans Affairs VA San Francisco Healthcare System, CA is seeking Architectural/Engineering Firms to submit Standard Form (SF) 330 for Project 662-25-105, Design Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT. The project will be located at the San Francisco VA Campus, 4150 Clement St, San Francisco, California 94121. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The requirement is for Project 662-25-105 Renovate Outpatient Clinics to PACT at the San Francisco VA Medical Center, Building 203 Ground Floor A-Wing, to provide A/E design services to renovate 13,750 SF of existing Outpatient Mental Health, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and VA Police Service space into a modern Hemodialysis Clinic and Women's Clinic plus renovated police and specialty care areas, supporting the long-term plan to consolidate inpatient care to the 2nd and 3rd floors, with an estimated construction cost of $15.7M, requiring a 2-day on-site design charrette, site investigations, block diagrams, and full design deliverables at 35%, 65%, 95%, 100% and final production per VA Master Specs and all applicable codes, including cost estimates, phased construction documents, and 5-year construction period services including RFI responses, submittal reviews, weekly meetings, site inspections, and as-builts, all to be completed within a 400-day design period. The design shall also substantially meet the VA design criteria as listed in VA design guides and manuals which can be found on the web at the VA Office of Facilities Management technical information library site address; http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL The design effort shall also include review of and assurance of compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act, including development and submission of all documents, reports, and activities necessary to obtain the required compliance. The contract work requires multiple disciplines. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm, and the lead designer in each discipline must be registered but neither need to be registered in California. The disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Interior Design, Structural, HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, Fire Protection, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Wayfinding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Include any additional disciplines that may be necessary on the SF 330. SF 330 Part 1F Example Projects; present all relevant VA projects first. Include in block 21 the contract number for all federal projects. Do not include the CPARS reports for federal projects. SELECTION CRITERIA Selection of firms for interviews and negotiations shall be based on an evaluation of the submitted SF 330s on the basis of the selection criteria listed below in a descending order of precedence. SF-330 s, Part I may be accompanied by any other evidence of experience and capabilities the applicant considers relevant. Part II shall be submitted for each proposed consultant s office involved. Selection Criteria descriptions are provided below. Past Experience of the prime firm, consultant firms and proposed designers. Prime firms must have proven experience in health care design through construction administration. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence in hospital design with the ability to design and administer projects within a complex, active healthcare environment with stringent seismic requirements in the State of California. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time and the ability to adhere to schedules. Provide current workload capability of the prime firm, proposed consultants and designers. Literature should be included to demonstrate the prime firm s ability to meet scheduled deadlines. This will allow the Government to determine the availability of experienced personnel during the performance period of the contract as well as the capacity to complete the work required. Past Performance on contracts with respect to cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules during design and construction phases (prime firm). Geographical location and knowledge of the locality of the project. This requirement considers the prime firm s familiarity with the applicable geographic area s architectural standards and codes, building codes, environmental regulations, soil conditions, and seismic requirements within the San Francisco area. The prime firm must be able to respond to and be on-site within a four-hour window. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: No more than eighty (80) pages Font size no smaller than 10 Size of emails not to exceed 10 MB. If more than one email is sent, number emails in subject line as 1 of 2, 2 of 2. Completed and return VAAR 852.219-77 VA Notice of limitation on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (attached) Subject line of the email shall state Company Name | Response to 36C26122R0061 | email 1 of 2 (if necessary) In the body of the email include Prime Company Name; UEI Number, email address and phone number of primary point of contact DUE DATE FOR SF 330 Firms that meet the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit required SF 330 s by 3:00 P.M. Pacific Standard Time (PST) Monday, September 7, 2026, to Alex Arter at alex.arter@va.gov. It is the intent of the Contracting Officer to make a single firm-fixed price contract award under this solicitation.

title: Principal Multi-Domain Command & Control (MDC2) Subject Matter Expert
description: 1.0 DESCRIPTION The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Command, Control, Communications, and Battle Management (PAE C3BM), Operational Response Team (ORT) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis to conduct market research and identify potential sources capable of providing highly specialized Principal Multi-Domain Command & Control (MDC2) Subject Matter Expertise (SME) support. 2.0 REQUIREMENT OVERVIEW The primary objective of this effort is to facilitate the seamless tactical integration of Common Operating Picture and Common Tactical Picture (COP/CTP) architectures into the tactical edge of the Department of the Air Force Battle Network (DAFBN) and Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS). The Government is seeking industry capabilities regarding Principal MDC2 SMEs with a minimum of 10 years of extensive background in: Space superiority C2 systems (e.g., Kronos) and integrated space coordination (DARPA ABII). Priority kill-chain constructs across rapid acquisition (Space RCO), missile defense, and national intelligence. Development of GEO Rendezvous and Proximity Operations (RPO) planning tools. Multi-source sensemaking, automated Course of Action (CoA) generation, and on-orbit edge processing (Nebula/Space Cloud). Security Requirement: This effort requires personnel to possess active Top Secret (TS) clearances with Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) eligibility, the ability to be read into Special Access Programs (SAPs), and access to an ICD 705 accredited facility. 3.0 IMPORTANT NOTE TO INDUSTRY (CROSS-REFERENCE) The Government is concurrently releasing a separate RFI for Tactical Aviation SME Support. This specific notice is strictly for the Principal MDC2 SME (Space/Orbital C2) requirement. Please ensure you are reviewing the correct PWS and responding to the correct notice. 4.0 ATTACHMENTS Interested vendors must review the attached documents for full requirement details and submission instructions: Attachment 1: Request for Information (RFI) Attachment 2: Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) 5.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS This is an RFI only. This does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an indication that the Government will contract for the services discussed. All information submitted is strictly voluntary. Responses shall follow the formatting, page limits, and instruction guidelines detailed in Attachment 1 (RFI). Responses must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist listed below no later than 3:00 PM EST on 07 September 2026. 6.0 POINTS OF CONTACT Contracting Officer: Mr. Cahi Hardy | cahi.hardy@us.af.mil Contract Specialist: Mr. Ethan George | ethan.george.3@us.af.mil

title: 129th Tumbler Cups
description: The California Air National Guard (CA ANG) is issuing a Request for Quotes (RFQ) to qualified contractors to provide and deliver 1,000 custom-engraved 30 oz stainless steel tumbler cups to multiple military recruiting locations across California. This acquisition is a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Quoters shall provide pricing and technical quotes covering the following two distinct project components: Engraved Tumbler Cups: The contractor shall provide 1,000 double-wall vacuum insulated 30 oz stainless steel tumbler cups conforming to the minimum product specifications (BPA-free, dishwasher safe, FlowState 3-position lid, reusable straw, and comfort-grip handle). Each cup must be custom laser-engraved with the "California Air National Guard" logo centered on the front (approximately 2.5 by 1.5 inches). Split-Shipment Logistics & Distribution (F.O.B. Destination): The contractor shall coordinate and complete delivery of the exact split-shipment quantities to four (4) distinct California military recruiting offices: Sunnyvale (300 qty), Fresno (200 qty), Oxnard (200 qty), and March ARB (300 qty). title: Injectable Egg-Free Influenza Vaccine 2027
description: The Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support is soliciting for the supply of Injectable Egg-Free Influenza Vaccine for the 2027-2028 flu season. Approximately 300,000 doses are included in this requirement. (Quantities may increase or decrease pending receipt of final Service requirements.) The vaccines shall be in prefilled syringes presentation. The vaccine shall be FDA-approved for immunizing individuals 18 years and older. The formula for the 2027-2028 season shall be determined by the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee. Other specification data is included in the solicitation. Successful contractor must have FDA Approval, and the vaccine must be U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended. National Stock Numbers shall be established at the time of award. An indefinite quantity contract is proposed. The quantity indicated is an annual estimate only. The guaranteed minimum will be 75% of the annual estimate, and a contract maximum will be established at 150% of the annual estimate. Ordered quantities shall be delivered to the Defense Depot New Cumberland, PA. The contractor shall be capable of delivering 40% of the requirement by August 12, 2027, 25% by August 26, 2027, 25% by September 9, 2027, and the residual 10% by September 23, 2027. The Delivery Schedule shall apply to the estimated annual quantity. This delivery schedule is the preferred delivery schedule. Other delivery schedules may be considered. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and SAM.gov at https://www.sam.gov. Interested parties should contact Rosbert Jones (445-737-1254) (Rosbert.Jones@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of presolicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current projected solicitation date is October of 2026. DLA reserves the right to issue the solicitation before or after the projected solicitation date.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Award for the 25 Hour Enhanced Airborne Flight Recorder (EAFR) Golden Chassis
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, AN INVITATION FOR BIDS, OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS. FURTHER, IT DOES NOT REPRESENT A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO PAY FOR COSTS INCURRED IN PREPARATION AND SUBMISSION OF DATA OR ANY OTHER COSTS INCURRED IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. This is a Sources Sought Notice with the intent to award a sole source award to General Electric Aerospace (GE) under the authority of FAR 13.106-1 based on GE�s unique technical qualifications as the only manufacturer and provider of the 25 Hour Enhanced Airborne Flight Recorder (EAFR) Golden Chassis as described below. Notice is provided as information to the marketplace, market research, and is an invitation for any other qualified companies to express their interest in and demonstrate their capability to provide the equipment/software that performs the required functions. Background The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is an independent federal agency charged by Congress with investigating every civil aviation accident in the United States and significant events in the other modes of transportation�railroad, transit, highway, marine, pipeline, and commercial space. We determine the probable causes of the accidents and events we investigate and issue safety recommendations aimed at preventing future occurrences. In addition, we conduct transportation safety research studies and offer information and other assistance to family members and survivors for each accident or event we investigate. We also serve as the appellate authority for enforcement actions involving aviation and mariner certificates issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and US Coast Guard, and we adjudicate appeals of civil penalty actions taken by the FAA. The NTSB�s Office of Research and Engineering, Vehicle Recorder Division (RE-40) requires the capability to download data from a variety of vehicle recording devices, especially flight data recorders (FDR) and cockpit voice recorders (CVR) from aircraft involved in aviation accidents. These systems require proprietary hardware and software from the manufacturer to download data. The 25 Hour EAFR and associated download equipment is designed and manufactured by GE and is required to download data from undamaged and damaged EAFR�s recovered from aircraft involved in accidents investigated by the NTSB. The GE product is proprietary and is not sold through any third-party resellers nor is it available for purchase through any government-wide acquisition vehicles. No other commercially available products are available currently that provide the same functionality. The EAFR download equipment are considered the definitive method of downloading data from the GE EAFR among industry professionals. Required Capabilities The NTSB requires the 25 Hour Enhanced Airborne Flight Recorder (EAFR) Golden Chassis. Sources capable of fully satisfying the above requirements are invited to submit capability statements/expressions of interest providing the Government the necessary information to determine actual capability. At a minimum, this information, which must be prepared specifically in response to this notice should, must include: (1) identification of company or organization; (2) an assertion of existing, full capability to meet proposed requirements; (3) business/contracts/marketing office point(s) of contact; (4) notification of business size and/or special status; and (5) any additional information that may be useful to the successful procurement of the requirements, if solicited. These expressions of interest shall adhere to a ten (10)-page submission limit plus web links and any specialized product descriptions. The statement of qualifications should include only information that clearly demonstrates the respondent's capabilities, expertise, and experience to perform the requirements described in this notice. General marketing material should not be included. The NTSB prefers that companies do not submit proprietary material. However, the Government recognizes that proprietary data may be a part of your submittal. If so, clearly mark such restricted or proprietary data and present it as an addendum to the non-restricted/non-proprietary information. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed order based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by NTSB. Parties must submit information within five (5) days of publication of this notice. NTSB will not return capability statements and the supporting documentation submitted in response to this notice. Telephone responses and inquiries will not be accepted. You may email questions regarding this notice to the issuing office to Nicole Evanitsky via email at: nicole.evanitsky@ntsb.gov

description: *The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition & Grants Office (AGO), Management and Budget Acquisition Office (OMB), intends to negotiate, on a sole source basis, under authority of FAR 12.102(a) and 41 USC 190, with Illumina. The requirement is for the purchase of reagents and supplies for the Illumina MiSeq i100 and i100 Plus Next-Generation Sequencing Systems, and training for laboratory personnel. ***The sole source determination is based on NOAA�s requirement for reagents, supplies, and training compatible with the Illumina MiSeq i100 and i100 Plus systems, which are critical for the Genetics and Evolution (GE) Program�s Molecular Genetics group. Stated Vendor is the only entity able to execute the desired services, as Illumina is the sole manufacturer of the i100/i100 Plus sequencers and all of their components and reagents, and the only provider of the required training. NOAA�s Northwest Fisheries Science Center (NWFSC) utilizes a wide variety of Illumina tools and integrated systems for large-scale analysis of genetic material. These supplies are required to fulfill mission-critical research for molecular genetics, forensics, and other related research. This science supports the conservation and management of marine and anadromous species, from deep-sea corals to salmon and whales, providing essential information for managing sustainable fisheries and conserving protected species. Additionally, training for laboratory personnel in the use and maintenance of the Illumina i100 and i100 Plus sequencers is required, as these are newly developed instruments and training must be provided by the original manufacturer. ***This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available.
